criteria.name: Functionality (detection, misses, false alarms, robustness, unseen data)
reasons: Reproduced: my full screen of 84c76b1 (/data/work/judge_A2_full) matches the recorded /data/work/final3 on all 15,269 per-frame outputs (only timing fields differ) and on every section of summary.json. Gated against the P3d baseline (regression_baseline_2026-09-26_ride_p3d.json) it passes: 38 gated metrics better, 0 worse, no --allow.

Real positives in doubleT_obstacle: my own count over the per-frame outputs gives the crossing person 61/61 (P3d 58/61). The first alarm is at frame 8, the first frame the person is labelled in-gauge (P3d: frame 11). The rail object is unchanged. In CI run 242, the original bag played through the Docker node gives STOP at 55.5–56.5 m, first STOP at +0.8 s.

Set O, re-scored per object with my own looser matcher: all 8 in-envelope objects get STOP. The edge cube goes from 2 to 18 frames (first STOP 5.2 to 35.0 m). The edge 2x2 box goes from 6 to 15 frames (first STOP 10.3 to 28.2 m). Other first STOPs: box at the envelope top 101.3 to 111.4 m, plank 82.2 to 87.2 m, floating cube 52.5 to 55.8 m. Background STOPs fall from 3 to 0. The outside box #7 keeps 8 false STOP frames at about 142 m (6 by the team's scorer).

Union envelope safety, re-derived by me: a quick screen with gauge.reference=0 compared frame by frame with the shipped run shows 0 frames on any of the 7 recordings where the rails alone STOP and the union does not. The union adds 23 set O frames and 3 person frames, and 0 on the empty recordings. My side-person injections at ±1.05 m give identical results with the union and with the rails alone (0–50 m 129/129; 50–100 m 96/126 and 99/126).

False alarms are still substantial. Ride (18.8 min, 13 km): 24 STOP tracks, 25 STOP episodes, 95 alarm frames (P3d 45/38/183), recounted from the JSONL. Five empty recordings: 9 events, 11 episodes, 37 frames; squareT_platform alone has 10 STOP episodes in 877 frames. The history stress gives 51 false STOP events over 33 histories (P3d 78), with 0 on the captured node histories.

Most of the ride gain is in-sample. With the opinion off (abl_noop, consistent with my own checks) the ride is 43/35. The opinion's own grouped held-out simulation keeps 33 of 42 events, so on unseen rides expect about 2.5 events per km.

Weak spots I measured: a person 0.1 m inside the envelope edge (centre ±1.2 m) gets STOP in only 82–84 of 129 frames at 0–50 m and 0 of 126 at 50–100 m from the rails (the union helps one side only: 128/129 and 3/126). The set F 0.5 m box is detected in 1 of 6 sequences. 0.3 m cubes get STOP only from 35–56 m.
missing: A real reduction of false STOPs that is not trained on the same ride, validated on a held-out ride or route
Better recall for objects just inside the envelope edge beyond 35 m, on both sides
Small objects beyond about 55 m; the outside box #7's false STOP frames

reasons: The method models the environment (rails, walls, envelope) rather than learning object appearance, which is what the organizers ask for.

Pre-registered held-out placement (/data/work/novel_final3.json): 723 of 2,458 visible frames (29.4%) against P3d's 544 (22.1%); 45 of 72 cases (unchanged); 0 paired-control matches; 23 cases better, 2 worse (−3 and −1 frames). In-sample dependence: the ride and history gains come from an opinion whose negatives are those same recordings (held-out AUC 0.974 on 200 negative rows; grouped simulation 42 to 33 ride events). The edge-object and person gains come entirely from the organizers' sensor-axis placement frame (with reference=0 I reproduce 5.2 m, 10.3 m and 58/61). Rules are tuned on the 7 recordings. There is no real held-out obstacle data.

criteria.name: Ease of launch
reasons: The documented chain is docker load, then docker run ... detector.launch.py, then ros2 bag play, then ros2 topic echo /resense/decision. CI verifies it the organizers' way: a uid-1000 player in another container, stock Fast DDS, --network none / internal network, and an offline docker save/load. docker-compose profiles also exist.

criteria.name: Generalization
reasons: The approach exploits the tunnel environment (rails, walls, train envelope), as the specification encourages.

The cycle adds in-sample machinery. The learned opinion's negatives are the very recordings it is scored on. Its threshold 0.0222 is chosen as the highest that delays no held-out synthetic positive (zero margin). Its held-out effect is modest: 42 -> 33 events, or 42 -> 38 at a 2x margin.

The model was trained at 64d6476 on the first integrated detector and not retrained after 65c5a5b changed the tracks it sees. The P2 agent's own report says it must be retrained whenever upstream stages change.

Most importance sits on lateral spread (lat_std 0.46). Per experiment_reports.json, adding crossing persons to training 'made separation worse', so they were kept only as a 10-sequence held-out test (none delayed). The cycle record does not mention this.

The union reference's gains rely on the organizers' sensor-axis placement frame. It widens only: rails median -0.20 to -0.29 deg; doubleT_obstacle -1.16 deg, reproduced from the per-frame yaw. The ride and five-empty rows are unchanged by it (abl_noref), so it has no measured false-alarm cost.
floating_free_max_dy 0.95 -> 1.2 and the reference range/offset values were sized on set O edge objects.

Positives: the pre-registered placement study improved (23 better / 2 worse, 0 controls). Of the 183 gained frames, 139 are within 60 m, where the sensor-axis union also acts, so the study does not separate rails-frame gains. My 24 out-of-distribution sequences show no regression and no gain versus P3d.
missing: A held-out false-alarm estimate for the shipped detector, and an opinion threshold with a margin (or with crossing and lying-person positives).
An answer to organizer question Q1 (rails or sensor axis), or a rails-frame justification of the edge gains.
A placement ablation with gauge.reference 0 to split the held-out gain.
Fewer rules fitted to the same six recordings and the ride.

The detector files are sealed (the freeze is verified in CI) and are identical between 65c5a5b and 84c76b1.

Design: the union is correctly non-narrowing. The profile is a symmetric rectangle, and every shape rule is monotone in |dy| (column needs off-centre or width >= 0.25 m, floating needs off-centre, the free exemption and wall_face read |dy|, edge and linear read the rails). Opinion withholds are bounded: at most 10 per track across all recordings.

The accumulation-buffer 'undo' of the union mis-recovers the rails lateral for buffered points within |c| of the centre (at most 0.2 m, far points only).

criteria.name: Ease of launch
reasons: An offline image archive and the documented chain (docker load -> docker run -> ros2 bag play -> ros2 topic echo). CI verifies the organizers' two-container chain, a stock uid-1000 player, no-network runs and the cold-disk original bags on 84c76b1.

Launch still needs some magic: a host sysctl for the UDP buffer, --net=host --ipc=host, freshness_mode:=replay, and --read-ahead-queue-size 10 (Humble's default cold burst is unsupported). A consumer must read the freshness fields.
The README's 'where to get the archive' points at another branch's CI artifact. The release is on hold by the user's decision, so I do not penalize it.
missing: Fewer required flags (a wrapper that sets the sysctl and flags).
A published archive for the reviewed commit, once the hold lifts.

criteria.name: Team approach
reasons: Five parallel candidate experiments behind opt-in keys, each screened by the same gate. Failures are documented (M2 and M4, a 2x-margin threshold, doubt_near 35, zone_min_votes, start_clean, axis_disagree_hold, a logistic blob scorer).
The 72-case placement plan was re-registered in 36c9d72 before its run (the hash matches).

The independent review was acted on and I verified each claim. Mode 3 union: side person 92/92 on both sides. Far-evidence tracks advisory, never hidden. A lifetime budget of 10 frames (maximum 10 per track in the data). The standing-body exemption: #6 is STOP from 28.7 m. Per-frame withhold counts: 0 on doubleT_obstacle; 3 on set O, at 129-141 m and not on a labelled in-envelope object. Per-mechanism ablations reproduce the attribution table exactly.
In-sample status is stated for the headline figures.

Minor: the phrase 'roughly a fifth of the ride gain survives' is arithmetically muddled (held-out, the opinion removes about half of its in-sample 19-event gain). Crossing-person separation and the selection of gate-passing variants among failed ones are left out of the cycle record.
missing: The crossing-person finding and the untrained-kind risk stated in the cycle record itself.
A held-out re-estimate after the fixes.

criteria.name: Pitch
reasons: The deck follows problem -> idea -> algorithm -> demo -> results. Every number carries a real / organizers' synthetic / our synthetic tag. The opinion is described honestly (at most about 1 s, in-sample 24 vs held-out 33).
The 2:50 video shows the jury chain and the person at 55.8 m; its narration matches the verified figures.
Deck slides 2-3 still contain template placeholders (<ФИО>, <Имя Фамилия>, <@ник>, <место учёбы>).
The video's clips (dated 10:57) predate the 27.09 detector.
Stale figures: 148 m from 24.09, and PRESENTATION.md:465 quotes a 'held from 149 m' that README:272 says must not be quoted.
missing: Filled team slides.
Footage re-recorded with the shipped detector.
Consistent current range figures.

checks_run.result: Numbers mostly consistent and labelled. Placeholders remain on deck slides 2-3; there are stale 148/149 m and 41 % CAUTION figures, and the set F 0.5 m box weakness is absent from the README results.

claims_found_wrong_or_overstated: 'Never delayed within 25 m' (QUALITY_CYCLE, config, deck) is false on missed frames. final3 JSONL shows 'doubt' detections at 24.7 m (new_data_1 track 295, frame 1262) and 25.0 m (new_data_2 track 570, frame 1337), because Tracker._doubt's miss branch keeps withholding without checking doubt_near. The effect is one frame each, on false tracks.

'Docstrings and config comments ... corrected' is not true for far evidence. configs/default.yaml:227, ros2_ws/.../detector.yaml:227, resense/config.py:355 and resense/tracking.py:37 and :356 still say 'not reported before: not reported', the pre-fix behaviour that the code no longer has. detector.py:527 still says stop_keep_thin is 'off by default'.

'tests/test_far_thin.py asserts the standing object is reported' is overstated. The test asserts only that it is not a STOP; the behaviour itself is correct (my probe shows it is reported as advisory).

'The held-out simulation keeps 33 of the rules' 42 ride events' describes the model trained at 64d6476 on the first integrated detector. It was not re-derived after 65c5a5b and uses a zero-margin threshold; at a 2x margin the simulation keeps 38 of 42.

'Roughly a fifth of the ride gain survives on unseen pieces' is arithmetically muddled. Held-out, the opinion removes 9 of 42 events (21 % of events), which is about half of its in-sample 19-event gain.
The cycle record omits that training on crossing persons worsened the opinion's separation (experiment_reports.json), although lateral spread is the model's dominant feature.

Stale figures. The deck and video quote the 24.09 person range of 148 m while the gate reads 151 m. PRESENTATION.md:465 quotes the 'held from 149 m' that README:272 says must not be quoted. README:308 says CAUTION on 41 % of the ride frames; the measured figure is 42.4 % (42.1 % in P3d).
The README results table omits the set F 0.5 m box: 1 of 6 detected, 18/110 frames within 50 m.

The placement study, presented as the held-out check, places objects in the organizers' sensor-axis frame. 139 of the 183 gained frames are within 60 m, where the sensor-axis union acts, so the study does not show rails-frame generalization.
safety_concerns: Learned delay. The opinion can hold a real object's STOP as CAUTION for up to 10 frames (about 1 s at 10 Hz, longer at lower input rates) beyond 25 m for clusters under 1 m tall, or beyond 40 m for any cluster. Its threshold sits at zero margin to the held-out synthetic positives. Crossing persons beyond 40 m and untrained kinds (lying person, debris) are plausible adversarial cases; the dominant feature is lateral spread.

Column width trim is a new demotion. A cluster taller than 2.2 m with a box 1.0-1.35 m wide and sparse tails becomes a 'column', and column_hold 2 keeps its track advisory. No positive test object is taller than 2.2 m, so this path is untested on positives.

Far evidence. far_evidence is sticky. A track whose zone vote needs far scan-line or weak hits stays advisory without an approach (e.g. at a standing train). Set F 1 m box loses 2 STOP frames at 83-85 m.

Union reference. Its gains rest on the organizers' sensor-axis frame (organizer question Q1 unanswered). It widens the envelope by up to 0.2 m within 60 m on straight track, with a step at 60 m. It never narrows (verified in code and by my side-person re-run), and no false-alarm cost was measured.
Miss-frame withholding at a predicted 24.7 m, inside the stated 25 m bound.
ROS path on 360-degree input (CI runner, 84c76b1): decode+detect p95 81 ms against a 100 ms period; the cold-start catch-up took 19.3 s before the node was on the newest frame.
Pre-existing blind spot: small objects on the bed between the rails are missed (0.3 m cube and plank 0/6, 0.5 m box 1/6), and the cycle does not address it.
